en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-Second Chapter
The Discourse on Momentariness: Are all phenomena momentary, lasting for only a single thought-moment?
Yes, they are.

Does the great earth remain stable because of the mind; does the great ocean remain stable; does Sineru, the king of mountains, remain stable; do water, fire, and air remain stable; and do grasses, shrubs, forests, and trees remain stable?
One should not say so… [as before]… Are all phenomena momentary, lasting for only a single thought-moment?
“Yes.
“Then you must not say that the eye-base is co-nascent with eye-consciousness. … [and so on] …
Is the eye-base co-nascent with eye-consciousness?
Yes. But did not the Venerable Sāriputta say this:—

“Friends, if the internal eye is intact, but external forms do not come into its range, and there is no corresponding act of attention, then the manifestation of the corresponding portion of consciousness does not occur.

Friends, if the internal eye is intact and external forms come into its range, but there is no corresponding act of attention, then the manifestation of the corresponding portion of consciousness does not occur.”

"But when, friends, the internal eye is intact, external forms come into its range, and there is the corresponding application of attention, then the manifestation of the corresponding portion of consciousness occurs.
Is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said that "the eye-base is co-nascent with eye-consciousness.
[The same applies to] the ear-base, and so forth.
Is the nose-base …pe… the tongue-base …pe… the body-base co-nascent with body-consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the body-base co-nascent with body-consciousness? Yes.
Did not the Venerable Sāriputta say this:
"Friends, when the internal body is intact but external tactile objects do not come into its range... [and so on] ...
friends, when the internal body is intact and external tactile objects do come into its range, yet... [and so on]?

"But, friend, when the internal body is intact and external tactile objects come into its range, and there is the corresponding attention, then the manifestation of the corresponding portion of consciousness occurs.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, it should not be said that "the body-base is co-nascent with body-consciousness.
It should not be said.
“Are all phenomena momentary, lasting for only a single thought-moment?”— Yes.
“Then are all phenomena permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change?”
It should not be said so.
Therefore, all phenomena are momentary, lasting for only a single thought-moment.
The Discussion on Momentariness is concluded.

The Twenty-second Chapter. Its summary (uddāna): There is parinibbāna without having abandoned some fetters; there is parinibbāna with some fetters remaining; there is parinibbāna after the fall [from the higher realms]; there is parinibbāna upon landing; there is parinibbāna without exertion; there is parinibbāna with exertion; there is parinibbāna in the interval; there is parinibbāna upon landing; there is parinibbāna after the fall; there is parinibbāna with the body remaining; there is parinibbāna without the body remaining; there is parinibbāna with perception; there is parinibbāna without perception; there is parinibbāna with neither-perception-nor-non-perception; there is parinibbāna through the cessation of perception and feeling; there is parinibbāna by means of the attainment of cessation; there is parinibbāna by means of the attainment of fruition. This is the summary of the twenty-second chapter.
The arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains final nibbāna;
the arahant, established in the imperturbable, attains final nibbāna;
there is the realization of the Dhamma even while lying in the womb.
There is the attainment of Arahatship while lying in the womb;
there is the realization of the Dhamma while dreaming;
there is the attainment of Arahatship while dreaming.
The mind of one who has gone into a dream is indeterminate;
there is no conditionality of repetition,
for all phenomena last for only a single moment of consciousness.
